posts.title: Weights Are a Compilation Target (Complexity Pt.5)
posts.description: TL;DR: A team at MIT CSAIL asked OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra to write small game-playing networks from the game rules and source code, with no task data, no gradient training and no practice games. Its Breakout network scored 517.4. The authors’ PPO baseline, trained for 500 million steps, scored 25.3. posts.title: The Engine Still Isn't the Car
posts.description: TL;DR: In 2024 I argued that the model is the engine of a generative AI application, and that nobody buys a car for its engine. For agents that still holds, but the question now sits one level higher. An enterprise with many teams needs a car platform, a shared layer that governs models, tools, identity and releases, so each team can build its own car on top of it.
